title: Daniel Siad, Model Scout Named 2,000 Times in Epstein Files, Found Dead in France
excerpt: The 69-year-old French modeling recruiter, who was under investigation for allegedly helping Jeffrey Epstein traffic young women across Europe, was discovered dead at his home near Paris. French prosecutors say the broader probe will continue.
body:
• Daniel Siad, a model scout linked to Jeffrey Epstein, was found dead in Colombes, France, with an autopsy pending to determine the cause of death.
  • Siad's name appeared over 2,000 times in Epstein files, and he was under investigation for trafficking young women.
  • Twenty-four women have come forward as victims or witnesses in the ongoing French investigation related to Siad.
  • Siad is the second individual connected to Epstein to die in France, following Jean-Luc Brunel's death in 2022.
Key Takeaways
  • Daniel Siad, 69, was found dead in Colombes, France; an autopsy is pending.
  • Siad's name appeared over 2,000 times in Epstein files; he was under investigation for trafficking.
  • 24 women have come forward as victims or witnesses in the ongoing French investigation.
  • Siad is the second Epstein-linked individual to die in France; Jean-Luc Brunel died in 2022.
  • The investigation will continue with about 10 investigators despite Siad's death.

Modeling Scout Found Dead Near Paris

Daniel Siad, a French professional model recruiter accused of spending more than a decade introducing young women to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, was found dead at his home in Colombes, a suburb northwest of Paris, on Monday evening, French prosecutors confirmed on Wednesday.

https://x.com/radar_online/status/2079951986485571661

The Nanterre prosecutor's office told Reuters that an autopsy will be carried out to determine the cause of death. Siad's body was discovered by a young woman he was living with, according to the Wall Street Journal. His lawyer, Ménya Arab-Tigrine, told Reuters she suspected he died of a heart attack, attributing it partly to months of intense media scrutiny.

"The stigma cast upon him — and by extension, his loved ones — and the daily pressure and anxiety he endured undoubtedly played a role. We must await the autopsy results to confirm whether his body simply gave out."

— Ménya Arab-Tigrine, Siad's lawyer

A Central Figure in the Epstein Files

Siad's name appeared more than 2,000 times in the Epstein files released by the U.S. Department of Justice in January 2026, according to French broadcaster BFMTV. The documents revealed he had communicated with Epstein from at least 2009 through 2018, frequently sending photos of young women he encountered while scouting models across Europe, North Africa, and beyond.

In one email from April 2009 included in the DOJ files, Siad sent Epstein a photo of a 17-year-old Slovakian girl he had found while scouting in Bratislava, according to People magazine. In another exchange from 2014, Siad compared his recruiting work to fishing: "In This busyness I feel like fisherman some time I cache quick, some time no fish," he wrote. Epstein paid Siad tens of thousands of dollars over the years, CNN reported.

The DOJ files also showed Siad recruiting across Poland, the Czech Republic, South Africa, Morocco, Cuba, and France, per The Sun. He organized auditions for Epstein during his Paris visits and claimed to have introduced between 10 and 15 models to the financier, according to the Wall Street Journal.

![Epstein Files. Siad's name appeared over 2,000 times in Epstein files; he was under investigation for trafficking.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Epstein_Files_Phase_1%2C_Part_C_%E2%80%93_Contact_Book_Redacted.pdf/page1-1280px-Epstein_Files_Phase_1%2C_Part_C_%E2%80%93_Contact_Book_Redacted.pdf.jpg)

Investigation Was Closing In

French authorities launched a wide-ranging probe into human trafficking, criminal conspiracy, and tax fraud in February 2026 following the release of the Epstein files. Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said on Wednesday that 24 women have since come forward as victims or witnesses of alleged acts committed by Siad or others in the network.

As part of the investigation, Siad was subjected to special investigative measures including phone taps, but prosecutors said the surveillance had not yielded enough evidence to justify his immediate arrest. At least five women had accused him directly of rape and human trafficking, according to French media reports cited by Reuters.

Siad consistently denied wrongdoing. In a CNN interview published in June, he insisted his relationship with Epstein was "strictly professional" and that he had no knowledge women he referred were being abused.

"I trusted him and believed this guy was a professional person. I never heard anything from anyone I introduced to him who came back to me that they had a bad situation."

— Daniel Siad, in a CNN interview, June 2026

Svetlana Pozhidaeva, a Russian-born model who told CNN that Siad introduced her to Epstein and that the financier abused her, responded to the news with frustration. "I wanted for justice to be served, for there to be some kind of investigation and achieve some closure," she told CNN on Wednesday.

Second Epstein-Linked Death in France

Siad is the second man publicly linked to Epstein's network to die in France. Jean-Luc Brunel, a prominent French modeling agent who was arrested in 2020 on charges of raping minors and sexual harassment, was found hanged in his Paris prison cell in February 2022 after 14 months in custody awaiting trial. Brunel denied the charges. The DOJ files contained dozens of emails between Siad, Epstein, and Brunel, and Siad had also recruited models for Brunel, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Epstein himself died in a New York jail cell in August 2019 while awaiting trial on federal sex trafficking charges. His death was ruled a suicide.

![Jeffrey Epstein. Timeline of Deaths Linked to Epstein 2019-08 Jeffrey Epstein dies in jail; ruled a suicide.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/59/Jeffrey_Epstein_mug_shot_%28cropped%29.jpg)

What Happens Next

The Paris prosecutor's office said the broader Epstein-related investigation will continue despite Siad's death, with approximately 10 investigators still working the case. At least 16 of the 24 women who have come forward have been formally interviewed, with additional interviews scheduled, according to CNN. The probe encompasses not just Siad but the wider network of individuals who may have facilitated Epstein's access to young women in France and across Europe.
